category_feedback.specific_evidence: Lesson Station B says pairs match equations to variable values 'without solving — just identify what the variable represents', but Worksheet Part 2 says 'Match each equation to the unknown number it stands for' with answer key 5+?=12 → 7, etc. The worksheet practises solving while the lesson defers it.
category_feedback.required_fix: Either rewrite Worksheet Part 2 so children match each equation to a description of the unknown ('the number that with 5 makes 12') without computing the value, OR revise lesson Station B step 2 to explicitly include solving. Align lesson activity, success criteria, and worksheet answer key.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.rationale names the variable-as-answer trap and recovery branches by what the child says ('If the child STILL says box = 7') but no named research citation appears. Rubric Level 4 example cites 'Ehri 2005 Phase 2' to ground the trap.
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite research grounding for variable-as-placeholder confusion in expanded_walkthrough.rationale — e.g., Kieran 1981 on the equal sign and variable misconception, or Knuth, Alibali, McNeil et al. 2006 on operational vs relational equal-sign understanding. One sentence linking the trap to the named source.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: lesson_specific_materials lists 'Magnifying Glass Variable Cards (24)' and 'Per-pair magnifying glass props (paper)' as required, and differentiation lacks a no-paper / no-purchase fallback path. Rubric Level 4 requires an explicit no-paper alternative usable on a zero-prep day.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a no-materials version to differentiation: e.g., 'No-prep version — teacher writes equations on the board and children make a fist (variable!) and an open hand (known number) to identify variables; no cards, no paper props needed.' Makes Lesson 1 runnable on any day.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Detective Dee anchors minds_on, action, and consolidation, and the chair metaphor is memorable, but consolidation.exit_routine is a sticky-note write task with no distinctive quotable refrain or sentence frame for children to carry between lessons. Rubric Level 4 wants a chant kids remember months later.
category_feedback.required_fix: Give Detective Dee a quotable closing chant tied to C2.1 — e.g., 'Variable, variable, hold the place — the unknown number fills the space!' Add it to consolidation.exit_routine as a class call-and-response that recurs in Lessons 2–5; reference it in the Lesson 1 teacher_script first.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Lesson treats equal sign as same-value-on-both-sides and frames variable as placeholder (Level 3 conceptual progression), but children only identify variables — they do not invent or compare strategies, and expanded_walkthrough does not name the misconception in research-grounded terms (Kieran on relational equality; Knuth et al. on operational vs relational).
category_feedback.required_fix: In action step 4 add an invent-and-compare beat: ask two pairs to show their Station C equations; class compares 'Did Pair A and Pair B use different symbols for the same kind of unknown? What stayed the same?' Then in expanded_walkthrough name the relational vs operational equal-sign distinction (Kieran 1981; Knuth et al. 2006).

summary: Pair 1 has strong alignment (C2.1 covered faithfully, expectation text byte-identical) but blocks on lesson_worksheet_consistency: Worksheet Part 2 asks for solved values while lesson Station B explicitly defers solving. Four other categories sit at 3 (no research citation, no no-paper fallback, no quotable refrain, no invent/compare beat). Revise both stages to align Part 2 with Station B and lift Lesson 1 to Level 4 on the named gaps.
